A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VeRO research and contain 30 readable pages, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A.1–A.5. The appendices are textually and visually identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments, cross-model transfer evaluations, and Pawn/Knight optimization case studies, including results in Tables 2–3 and appendix Tables 6–13.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark, transfer, and case-study results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The VeRO abstractions, scaffold configurations, and optimization procedure remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 is relocated without changes to its steps.

E1.justification: Both versions use GAIA, GPQA, MATH, TAU-Bench Retail, and SimpleQA for benchmarking, with FACTS Search also used in the case study. The target-model transfer scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same Claude Code Pure/VeRO Tools and VeRO Default/Orchestrator/Resources-Only configurations and optimizer-model comparisons. No comparator is added or removed from the corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: Dataset splits in Table 1, target models, temperature, checkpoint selection, evaluation metrics, and budgets remain unchanged, including B=8 for benchmarking and B=5 for the case study.

E4.justification: The scaffold/model ablations, transfer tests, instruction-template case study, and semantic trajectory analyses are retained without revisions in Sections 4–5 and Appendices A.2–A.3.

E5.justification: Both versions report N=3 for benchmark configurations and N=4 for case-study configurations. Seed-related statements and the reporting of means, maxima, standard deviations, and error bars are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and plotted findings match throughout. For example, Table 2 retains average scores of 0.61 for VeRO Default/Sonnet and 0.53 for Claude Code Pure/Sonnet; robustness and appendix results also match.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 retains the same task definitions, constrained optimization objectives, assumptions, and optimizer recurrence. Changes to equation delimiter typesetting preserve the mathematics.

C1.justification: The harness, benchmark, and empirical findings remain the same three contributions. Scientific claims in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain their meaning and scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of optimization headroom, instruction-dependent tradeoffs, and transfer failures are unchanged. Section 6 and Appendix A.4 retain the same methodological limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds the scaleapi/vero GitHub repository address in the abstract. v1 announces release without this access pointer; implementation and configuration documentation otherwise match. This establishes added access information, not verified repository contents.

R1.justification: The same 34 references and related-work discussions are retained, including the positioning relative to prompt optimization, ADAS, AFlow, and coding-agent benchmarks.

P1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability sentence and an ICML 2026 acceptance note, and updates the arXiv version/date text. The substantive prose and section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Algorithm 1 moves from page 5 to page 6, with associated text and table reflow and minor equation typesetting changes. Figures, table structures, and captions are retained; appendix layouts match exactly.

improvement.justification: The explicit repository address modestly improves code discoverability and reproducibility documentation compared with v1's release statement. Scientific evidence and limitations are unchanged; the acceptance note and layout shifts do not establish additional quality gains.
